decisions.reason: Using Danish style names does not change which style system must be implemented or its required coverage across the template set.

The client accepts the immediately preceding proposal that the document default will be English while style names will be Danish, changing the existing Danish default-language value and resolving the value conflict.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: That sounds great. When you're ready, please return with your approach, estimate, and anything you need to complete the project.

decisions.reason: The language used for style names does not change Tab-driven sublevel creation, list coverage, hierarchy behavior, or alignment.
Danish style naming does not alter bullet size, visual balance, vertical alignment, or scaling behavior.
The accepted language arrangement does not change the required stability of legacy-content pasting or its specified test files.
Style-name language does not change the required containment of pasted tables or right-hand columns within page margins.
The accepted language arrangement does not affect the requirement that manual line breaks work reliably after legacy-content pasting.
Danish style names and an English document default do not change the supported Word for Windows environment or general reliability expectations.
